judge_verdict.summary: The agent completed the full adaptability workflow, but the verifier scored only 4/7 oracle action matches and failed the rollout.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure: the adaptability LLM judge returned binary_reward 0 with a fractional score of 0.571429, which is exactly 4/7 and therefore below the implicit 1.0 pass bar for action-mode tasks [1][2], yet the agent substantively executed the entire conditional scenario the user requested [3]. After reading the prompt, the agent scheduled Friday lunch at 12:30–13:30 with all four dinner guests from last week [4], notified the user that lunch was booked [5], waited for and detected attendee deletions that triggered the backup plan [6], then scheduled the 6–8 PM Dinner and Game Night, ordered the Default cab 30 minutes beforehand, purchased the ages-13+ Tic Tac Two item, and messaged the youngest attendee Saskia König [7][8]. The score shortfall comes from oracle-action mismatches the task itself allows or that are immaterial to outcomes: the reference sends via Messages with a phone user_id while the agent correctly fell back to Chats after Messages lookup returned empty, as the user instruction permits [3][9]; checkout was called with {} instead of an explicit empty discount_code despite succeeding [8][10]; and the agent's richer lunch and wrap-up user messages do not literally equal the oracle's terse "I have scheduled the lunch." even though they convey the required scheduling confirmation [5][11]. Those formatting and channel choices are verifier-oracle rigidity, not missing task work, so the FAIL does not reflect a genuinely unsolved rollout.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent scheduled lunch correctly but never adapted to the attendee cancellation, so it missed dinner, cab, shopping, and messaging actions the adaptability scenario requires.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. The adaptability verifier compares the agent's write-actions against a seven-step oracle cascade triggered when a lunch attendee cancels, requiring dinner scheduling, a cab ride, game purchase, a message to the youngest attendee, and a user reply of "I have scheduled the lunch." [2][3][4] The verifier reported binary_reward 0 after action-mode grading [1]. The agent did read the multi-step request and correctly created the Friday lunch with the four dinner attendees from last week [5][6], but then failed to detect the simulated cancellation: its first `are_wait_for_notification` call was aborted by a 120-second harness tool timeout despite requesting 900 seconds [7], after which it switched to `SystemApp__wait_for_notification`—not the instructed ARE wait tool—and polled email and chat inboxes that contained no cancellation [8][9]. Concluding no cancellation occurred, it sent only a verbose status message to the user and never scheduled dinner and game night, ordered the cab or Tic Tac Two game, or messaged Saskia König [10], leaving one lunch creation and one user message where seven matched write-actions were required. The agent's own checks were therefore insufficient for an adaptability task that depended on properly waiting for environment notifications rather than inferring absence from unrelated inboxes.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent completed the full adaptability chain (lunch, cancellation wait, dinner, cab, game purchase, youngest-attendee notice) but failed verification because it sent three user-facing messages when the scorer allows at most two.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure on an otherwise complete adaptability run: the held-out scorer reported binary_reward 0 with continuous reward 0.0 [1][2], using adaptability action-mode judging that requires matching seven oracle write actions and permits at most one extra AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user beyond the single oracle notification [3][4][5]. The user task demanded scheduling Friday lunch with last week's dinner guests, notifying when done, then—if attendees cancel—scheduling a 6PM dinner/game night, ordering a cab 30 minutes prior, buying the ages-13+ Tic Tac Two game, and messaging the youngest attendee via Messages or Chats as fallback [6]. The agent executed that chain: it created the 12:30–13:30 lunch with the four correct attendees [7], told the user lunch was scheduled [8], waited and received calendar deletions from Věra Nováková and Saskia König [9], created the 18:00–20:00 Dinner and Game Night with the same four people [10], booked a Default cab from Charles University at 17:30 to the user's home address [11], added oracle item c17fd59a68e44af4af3d4197a7591846 and checked out [12], found Messages empty for Saskia König and correctly fell back to Chats to notify the youngest attendee about the game [13][14], matching the reference oracle's substantive calendar, cab, shopping, and messaging sequence [15]. The failure is mechanical: the agent issued three send_message_to_user calls (steps 6, 18, and 19) while the verifier allows only two (oracle count 1 plus one extra) [16][17], which forces reward to 0.0 regardless of action matching [5]; those two closing summaries were not required by the task and breached the prompt's 'only when required' reply rule [18], but they do not undo the correctly completed scheduling, shopping, ride, and attendee-notification work.
